gloss: outbreak of fire; fire breaking out

definitions.gloss: outbreak of fire; fire breaking out
definitions.explanation: The start or occurrence of a fire, especially in buildings or structures.

examples.japanese: {深夜|しんや}に{出火|しゅっか}した。
examples.english: A fire broke out late at night.

examples.japanese: {出火|しゅっか}{原因|げんいん}はまだ{調査中|ちょうさちゅう}です。
examples.english: The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

examples.japanese: {台所|だいどころ}から{出火|しゅっか}し、{住宅|じゅうたく}{一棟|いっとう}が{全焼|ぜんしょう}したが、{幸|さいわ}いけが{人|にん}はいなかった。
examples.english: A fire broke out from the kitchen and one house was completely destroyed, but fortunately no one was injured.

notes:
Composed of {出|しゅつ} (come out, appear) + {火|か} (fire). A formal word commonly seen in news reports and fire department announcements. Used as both a noun and a suru verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出火|しゅっか}する: a fire breaks out
- {出火|しゅっか}{原因|げんいん}: cause of fire
- {出火|しゅっか}{元|もと}: source of fire, where the fire started
- {出火|しゅっか}{場所|ばしょ}: location where the fire broke out
- {出火|しゅっか}を{防|ふせ}ぐ: to prevent fire outbreaks

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
{出荷|しゅっか} (shipping, shipment) sounds the same but uses different kanji and has a completely different meaning.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {火事|かじ}: fire (as an event) — the general word for a fire
- {火災|かさい}: fire, conflagration — formal, used in reports and statistics
- {発火|はっか}: ignition, catching fire — the moment something catches fire
- {失火|しっか}: accidental fire — fire caused by negligence
